result.summary: Check whether a peer can be added as an orphan resolution candidate before performing parent lookups during wtxid announcements. The check tests whether the peer already announced the orphan or would exceed its announcement budget, using transaction input count as an upper bound for missing parents.
result.problem: When a peer announces an orphan transaction's wtxid, the node searches for missing parents across all inputs before determining if the peer can even be registered as a resolution candidate. Peers repeatedly announcing orphans with many inputs cause repeated redundant parent lookups on the message processing thread, even after reaching their announcement limit or having already announced the orphan.
evidence: Author benchmark in PR description: with 12 orphans containing 2,430 inputs each, processing an inv message announcing those 12 wtxids from an over-budget peer drops from 14.5–16.2 ms on master to 0.19–0.22 ms with this PR.
result.scope_notes: Very small patch (+8/-0). Diff was not provided in context.
result.card: Short-circuits missing-parent lookups for orphan wtxid announcements when the announcing peer cannot become an orphan resolution candidate. Peers that have already announced an orphan or exceeded their announcement limits currently force thousands of redundant parent lookups per announcement. The author reports inv processing times dropping from ~15 ms to ~0.2 ms for 12 large orphans on a synthetic test.
uncertainties: The diff was not provided to verify exact placement and lock acquisition order.

risk.why: A flaw in candidate filtering logic could prematurely reject valid peers during orphan resolution or leave orphans unresolvable.
